internal.description: Whether the calls the web pages make to the API in-process (about six for each page view) are written to the activity log as API lines: all, or off.
internal.title: Internal
internal.x-label: Log the pages' own API calls
internal.x-summary: All API calls are logged by default; off leaves out the ones the web pages make to themselves.

max_mb.description: How much disk the site's stored caches (today the Galaxy Map's nodes and stages) may use, in all. When it is full the warm-up stops, the nodes it built ahead stay, and the nodes a visit asked for are dropped, the least recently visited first (0 turns the disk caches off).
max_mb.title: Max Mb
max_mb.x-summary: How much disk the site's stored caches may use in all; 0 turns them off.

warm_on_change.description: Start the warm-up by itself after anything that changes what the site shows (a generation run, the orbital update, an edit), so the caches are rebuilt without waiting for the next update. It rebuilds only what the change touched.
warm_on_change.title: Warm On Change
warm_on_change.x-summary: Start the cache warm-up by itself after anything that changes what the site shows.

warm_settle_seconds.description: How long the automatic warm-up waits after the first change before it starts, so a burst of edits is one warm-up and not one for each.
warm_settle_seconds.title: Warm Settle Seconds
warm_settle_seconds.x-summary: How long the warm-up waits after a change, so a burst of edits is one rebuild.

apple_touch_icon.description: The 180 by 180 PNG iPhones and iPads use for a home-screen bookmark. Set it by uploading on the Images page.
apple_touch_icon.title: Apple Touch Icon
apple_touch_icon.x-summary: The icon iPhones and iPads use when the site is added to the home screen.

favicon_png.description: A PNG or ICO icon for browsers that do not take an SVG; empty offers none. Set it by uploading on the Images page.
favicon_png.title: Favicon Png
favicon_png.x-summary: A fallback icon for browsers that do not read SVG; upload it on the Images page.

favicon_svg.description: The site icon as an uploaded SVG; empty uses the built-in one. Set it by uploading on the Images page.
favicon_svg.title: Favicon Svg
favicon_svg.x-summary: The icon browsers show in tabs; upload it on the Images page.

manifest_enabled.description: Serve /site.webmanifest, which names the site, its icon and its theme colour for browsers that can install it.
manifest_enabled.title: Manifest Enabled
manifest_enabled.x-summary: Let browsers offer to install the site as an app.

dir.description: Where each background job's command lines, status and output are kept; empty means /var/lib/planetGen/jobs.
dir.title: Dir
dir.x-summary: Where each background job's command lines, status and output are kept.

keep.description: How many finished jobs are kept.
keep.title: Keep
keep.x-summary: How many finished jobs stay in the job list.

python.description: The interpreter that runs planetgen and planetgen.cli.reset for the jobs; empty means the web app's own Python. Editing it from the web would be code execution, so it is file-only.
python.title: Python
python.x-summary: The interpreter that runs the generation jobs; empty uses the web app's own.

database.description: The galaxy database the pages show and the generators fill.
database.title: Database
database.x-summary: The database the pages show and the generators fill.

database_prefix.description: The schema-name prefix the database picker lists, for a deployment with several galaxies on one server.
database_prefix.title: Database Prefix
database_prefix.x-summary: The name prefix the database picker lists, for several galaxies on one server.

host.description: The MySQL server's host name or address.
host.title: Host
host.x-summary: The address of the database server.

password.title: Password
password.x-summary: That account's password; it is never shown.

port.title: Port
port.x-summary: The port the database server listens on.

statement_timeout_seconds.description: The longest any statement on the web interface's and API's read-only connections may run (0 turns the limit off). A query it stops gives a 504 page, or a QUERY_TIMEOUT error from the API.
statement_timeout_seconds.title: Statement Timeout Seconds
statement_timeout_seconds.x-summary: How long a page or API query may run before it is stopped; 0 means no limit.

user.description: The account every entry point connects with; give it whatever grants the most demanding caller needs.
user.title: User
user.x-summary: The account every part of planetGen connects with.

card_cache_dir.description: Where drawn preview pictures are cached; empty means the state folder.
card_cache_dir.title: Card Cache Dir
card_cache_dir.x-summary: Where drawn preview pictures are kept.

card_cache_mb.description: How much disk the drawn preview pictures may use.
card_cache_mb.title: Card Cache Mb
card_cache_mb.x-summary: How much disk the drawn preview pictures may use.

default_image.description: The picture link previews show (a PNG or JPEG about 1200 by 630); empty uses the built-in one. Set it by uploading on the Images page.
default_image.title: Default Image
default_image.x-summary: The picture link previews show; upload it on the Images page.

enabled.description: Add Open Graph and Twitter tags to the public pages, so a link shows a title, a description and a picture when shared.
enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.x-summary: Show a title, description and picture when a link to the site is shared.

generated_cards.description: Draw a preview picture per system and sector instead of one for the whole site. Off until a card drawer is installed; every page then uses the default picture.
generated_cards.title: Generated Cards
generated_cards.x-summary: Draw a preview picture for each system and sector; off until a card drawer is installed.

image_alt.description: A description of the default preview picture for people who cannot see it.
image_alt.title: Image Alt
image_alt.x-summary: Describes the preview picture for people who cannot see it.

site_name.description: The site name in link previews; empty uses the site name.
site_name.title: Site Name
site_name.x-summary: The site name shown in link previews; empty uses the site name.

twitter_card.description: How X (Twitter) draws a preview: a large picture or a small one.
twitter_card.title: Twitter Card
twitter_card.x-summary: Whether X draws a large or a small preview picture.

twitter_site.description: The site's X (Twitter) account, as @name; empty names none.
twitter_site.title: Twitter Site
twitter_site.x-summary: The site's X account as @name; empty names none.

enabled.description: Keep the API's public answers in memory, per WSGI process.
enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.x-summary: Keep the API's public answers in memory so repeat requests are fast.

max_age_seconds.description: Nothing is kept longer than this.
max_age_seconds.title: Max Age Seconds
max_age_seconds.x-summary: No answer is kept in memory longer than this.

max_entries.title: Max Entries
max_entries.x-summary: The most answers kept in memory.

max_mb.description: Most memory the answers may take.
max_mb.title: Max Mb
max_mb.x-summary: The most memory the cached answers may use.

shared_seconds.description: How long an answer is kept in Redis, where every web process and the warm-up share it. Each answer is served only while the data it read has not changed, so this only bounds the memory.
shared_seconds.title: Shared Seconds
shared_seconds.x-summary: How long a shared answer is kept in Redis; it only bounds the memory.

stamp_seconds.description: How often the galaxy's content stamp is checked.
stamp_seconds.title: Stamp Seconds
stamp_seconds.x-summary: How often the galaxy's content stamp is checked.

stored_counts.description: Table pages show stored totals and filter-menu counts, refreshed in the background, instead of counting whole tables in the request (off: exact counts at any price).
stored_counts.title: Stored Counts
stored_counts.x-summary: Table pages show stored totals, refreshed in the background, instead of counting on each request.

warm_max_objects.description: Most sector pages, system pages and phenomenon pages the warm-up builds (each, nearest the galaxy centre first); the rest are built on their first visit, and the warm-up says how many it left out.
warm_max_objects.title: Warm Max Objects
warm_max_objects.x-summary: Most sector, system and phenomenon pages the warm-up builds; the rest build on first visit.

dir.description: Where the parity file is kept; empty means /var/lib/planetGen/parity. Keep it off the disk the database is on if you can: a parity file on the same failing disk protects nothing.
dir.title: Dir
dir.x-summary: Where the sector repair file is kept; empty uses /var/lib/planetGen/parity.

enabled.description: Keep a parity file beside the database that can rebuild a damaged sector: every saved or edited sector updates the parity of its group, which costs a few milliseconds a save and about 7 percent of the sectors' size in disk space. Off, saves write no parity and `planetgen refresh-parity` builds it later.
enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.x-summary: Keep a parity file that can rebuild a damaged sector; saves get a little slower.

group_size.description: Sectors in one parity group (G). Any `parity_blocks` damaged sectors of a group are rebuilt from the rest, which are read to do it: a bigger group costs less disk and more reading. A change applies to the groups made afterwards.
group_size.title: Group Size
group_size.x-summary: How many sectors share one set of parity blocks.

parity_blocks.description: Parity blocks per group (m): how many damaged sectors of one group can be rebuilt. A change applies to the groups made afterwards.
parity_blocks.title: Parity Blocks
parity_blocks.x-summary: How many damaged sectors of one group the repair file can rebuild.

memory_kib.description: Memory one admin password check uses, in KiB (Argon2id). 19456 (19 MiB) with time_cost 2 and parallelism 1 is OWASP's minimum; raise it where the host has the memory to spare. A stored hash made with other numbers is re-hashed at that admin's next sign-in.
memory_kib.title: Memory Kib
memory_kib.x-summary: How much memory checking one admin password takes; the default is OWASP's minimum.

parallelism.description: Threads one admin password check uses (Argon2id).
parallelism.title: Parallelism
parallelism.x-summary: How many threads one admin password check uses.

time_cost.description: Passes over that memory for one admin password check (Argon2id).
time_cost.title: Time Cost
time_cost.x-summary: How many passes one admin password check makes over its memory.

x_for.description: Reverse proxies to trust for X-Forwarded-For, the client address (0 = off).
x_for.title: X For
x_for.x-summary: How many reverse proxies to trust for the visitor's address (0 means none).

x_host.description: Reverse proxies to trust for X-Forwarded-Host (0 = off).
x_host.title: X Host
x_host.x-summary: How many reverse proxies to trust for the host name (0 means none).

x_proto.description: Reverse proxies to trust for X-Forwarded-Proto, the scheme (0 = off).
x_proto.title: X Proto
x_proto.x-summary: How many reverse proxies to trust for http or https (0 means none).

interactive_workers.description: How many workers are kept for short jobs: edits, estimates and slow page answers. They are never counted in the bulk worker count, so a generation run on every core leaves them be, and they run at a higher priority than the bulk workers.
interactive_workers.title: Interactive Workers
interactive_workers.x-summary: How many workers are reserved for short jobs; generation work never takes them.

long_job_seconds.description: A job expected to take longer than this goes to the long lane. A job with no estimate counts as short.
long_job_seconds.title: Long Job Seconds
long_job_seconds.x-summary: Jobs expected to take longer than this go to the long lane.

long_workers.description: How many workers run the jobs expected to take longer than the long job limit (a neighbourhood or a large settle, which can run for hours). They have a lane of their own so a long job can never hold the workers kept for short ones.
long_workers.title: Long Workers
long_workers.x-summary: How many workers run long jobs, apart from the ones for short jobs.

maintenance_workers.description: How many workers run the cache warm-up, the node prefetch and the database check while a generation run is live. They are taken out of the generation worker count (a generation worker finishes its unit and leaves when they are needed), so the host's total does not grow; with no generation run live they may use the whole count.
maintenance_workers.title: Maintenance Workers
maintenance_workers.x-label: Workers for upkeep during a run
maintenance_workers.x-summary: How many workers keep the caches and checks going while a generation run is live.

max_host_workers.description: The most worker processes planetgen may run on this host at once, every queue and command together: a start that would pass it is refused and said in the log. 0 sizes it from the host: 60 percent of its memory in workers of 300 MB each, no more than four per core, and never fewer than the cores plus four. It stops a burst of requests, or several commands starting workers together, from filling the memory and getting MySQL killed.
max_host_workers.title: Max Host Workers
max_host_workers.x-summary: The most worker processes planetgen runs at once on this host; 0 sizes it from memory and cores.

max_waiting.description: How many entries the one waiting list holds: generation runs and API jobs that wait for the machine, and Generate page jobs that wait for the running job. One more than this is refused, naming the list.
max_waiting.title: Max Waiting
max_waiting.x-summary: How many runs and jobs can wait for their turn at once; one more is refused.

unit_ceiling_seconds.description: The longest a unit of a generation stage is expected to run. A stage is cut into units no longer than this at the default galaxy size; a unit that runs longer is written to the run's log, naming the stage. A stage that is one unit by nature is not held to it. A unit this long is also the most a worker waits to hand its place to a lane that needs it.
unit_ceiling_seconds.title: Unit Ceiling Seconds
unit_ceiling_seconds.x-summary: The longest one unit of a generation stage is meant to run; a longer one is logged.

wait_minutes.description: How long a generation run, or an API job that generates sectors, waits in line when another generation run holds the machine, before it fails naming that run (0 does not wait).
wait_minutes.title: Wait Minutes
wait_minutes.x-summary: How long a run waits in line for the one in front of it before it gives up (0 means it does not wait).

default.description: Flask-Limiter's default limit for the API.
default.title: Default
default.x-summary: How many API requests each client may make; empty turns the limit off.

storage_uri.description: Where limits count; empty means the Redis server in redis.url, memory:// counts per process (right with exactly one worker).
storage_uri.title: Storage Uri
storage_uri.x-summary: Empty counts in Redis; memory:// counts per process.

galaxy.description: Limit on /galaxy, the Galaxy Map page. Empty turns it off.
galaxy.title: Galaxy
galaxy.x-summary: How often one visitor may open the Galaxy Map page; empty turns the limit off.

galaxy_tiles.description: Limit on /galaxy/nodes, /galaxy/stage, /galaxy/window, /galaxy/near and /galaxy/territories, fetched as the map's camera moves. Empty turns it off.
galaxy_tiles.title: Galaxy Tiles
galaxy_tiles.x-summary: How fast one visitor may load map data while moving the map; empty turns the limit off.

health.description: Limit on /api/health. Empty turns it off.
health.title: Health
health.x-summary: How often one client may call the health check; empty turns the limit off.

other.description: Limit on every other page, counted together. Empty turns it off.
other.title: Other
other.x-summary: How often one visitor may load any other page, counted together; empty turns the limit off.

search.description: Limit per client address on /search and /galaxy/locate. Empty turns it off.
search.title: Search
search.x-summary: How often one visitor may search; empty turns the limit off.

url.description: The Redis server the work queue, the rate limits and the login lockouts use.
url.title: Url
url.x-summary: The Redis server used by the work queue, the rate limits and the login lockouts.

block_ai_crawlers.description: Disallow the crawlers that collect text to train AI models (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended) in robots.txt.
block_ai_crawlers.title: Block Ai Crawlers
block_ai_crawlers.x-summary: Ask the crawlers that collect text to train AI models to stay away.

description.description: The description search engines show for pages that give none of their own (about 155 characters are shown); empty uses the tagline.
description.title: Description
description.x-summary: The snippet search engines show for pages without their own; empty uses the tagline.

detail_pages.description: Whether the generated system, sector and phenomenon pages may be indexed when indexing is top_pages. Millions of generated pages look like scaled content to search engines, so they stay out by default; a small galaxy can switch this to index.
detail_pages.title: Detail Pages
detail_pages.x-summary: Whether the generated system, sector and phenomenon pages may be indexed.

humans_txt.description: The text of /humans.txt; empty serves none.
humans_txt.title: Humans Txt
humans_txt.x-summary: The text served at /humans.txt; empty serves none.

indexing.description: Whether search engines may index the site: off (robots.txt disallows everything and every page says noindex), top_pages (the home, class, species, polity, galaxy and list pages), or all (also the system, sector and phenomenon pages).
indexing.title: Indexing
indexing.x-summary: Which pages search engines may list: none, the main pages, or all of them.

json_ld.description: Add a WebSite block (schema.org) to the home page.
json_ld.title: Json Ld
json_ld.x-summary: Add a website block to the home page so search engines understand the site.

keywords.description: Keywords for the keywords meta tag. Google has ignored it since 2009; some smaller engines still read it.
keywords.title: Keywords
keywords.x-summary: Words for the keywords tag; most search engines ignore them.

privacy_note.description: A short note shown on the account page about what the site keeps.
privacy_note.title: Privacy Note
privacy_note.x-summary: A short note on the account page about what the site keeps.

robots_extra.description: Lines added to the end of the generated robots.txt.
robots_extra.title: Robots Extra
robots_extra.x-summary: Lines added to the end of the generated robots.txt.

robots_override.description: Replaces the generated robots.txt entirely when not empty. A mistake here can hide the whole site from search engines.
robots_override.title: Robots Override
robots_override.x-summary: Replaces the whole generated robots.txt; a mistake can hide the site from search engines.

security_txt.description: The text of /.well-known/security.txt (RFC 9116 needs a Contact and an Expires line); empty serves none.
security_txt.title: Security Txt
security_txt.x-summary: The text served at /.well-known/security.txt; empty serves none.

sitemap_cache_hours.description: How long a built sitemap is reused.
sitemap_cache_hours.title: Sitemap Cache Hours
sitemap_cache_hours.x-summary: How long a built sitemap is reused before it is built again.

sitemap_enabled.description: Serve /sitemap.xml and list it in robots.txt.
sitemap_enabled.title: Sitemap Enabled
sitemap_enabled.x-summary: Publish /sitemap.xml and list it in robots.txt.

sitemap_max_urls.description: Most addresses in one sitemap file (the limit is 50,000).
sitemap_max_urls.title: Sitemap Max Urls
sitemap_max_urls.x-summary: The most addresses in one sitemap file (up to 50,000).

backups_kept.description: How many backup archives are kept. One is made just before every settings save, restore or import replaces the file, and by Back up now; the oldest is deleted once there are more than this, but never the newest archive that holds every part.
backups_kept.title: Backups Kept
backups_kept.x-summary: How many settings backup archives to keep; the oldest is deleted first.

language.description: The pages' language as a code (en, de, en-GB): the `lang` of every page and the Open Graph locale.
language.title: Language
language.x-summary: The language code of the pages, such as en or en-GB.

tagline.description: A short line shown under the home page's heading and used as the description of pages that give none of their own.
tagline.title: Tagline
tagline.x-summary: A short line under the home page heading, and the description of pages that have none.

dir.description: Where the Galaxy Map's nodes are cached on disk; empty means /var/cache/planetgen/tiles.
dir.title: Dir
dir.x-summary: Where the Galaxy Map's nodes are cached; empty uses /var/cache/planetgen/tiles.

prefetch_max_queued.description: The background build queues nothing while this many of its jobs (16 nodes each) or other upkeep work already wait.
prefetch_max_queued.title: Prefetch Max Queued
prefetch_max_queued.x-summary: The background build waits while this many of its jobs are already queued.

prefetch_per_minute.description: Most nodes the background build queues in a minute, all requests together.
prefetch_per_minute.title: Prefetch Per Minute
prefetch_per_minute.x-summary: Most nodes the background build queues in a minute, all visitors together.

prefetch_per_visit.description: Most nodes one request for nodes queues to be built in the background: the children of the nodes it asked for, then their parents and the parents' other children (0 turns the background build off).
prefetch_per_visit.title: Prefetch Per Visit
prefetch_per_visit.x-summary: Most nodes one visit queues to be built ahead in the background (0 turns it off).

warm_zoom_floor.description: Finest block level of the zoom run `planetgen warm` builds from the opening view in to the galaxy's centre, on top of the populated blocks it builds in full (9 is blocks of nine shells, about 36 pc across; the run covers blocks of that size and bigger; 243 or more builds no run).
warm_zoom_floor.title: Warm Zoom Floor
warm_zoom_floor.x-summary: How far in the map is prepared: blocks of this many shells; 243 or more skips it.

assets_dir.description: Where uploaded icons and images are kept; empty means the assets folder in the state folder.
assets_dir.title: Assets Dir
assets_dir.x-summary: Where uploaded icons and pictures are stored.

theme_color_dark.description: The same for the dark theme.
theme_color_dark.title: Theme Color Dark
theme_color_dark.x-summary: The toolbar colour phones show with the dark theme.

theme_color_light.description: The browser's toolbar colour on phones for the light theme, as #rrggbb.
theme_color_light.title: Theme Color Light
theme_color_light.x-summary: The toolbar colour phones show with the light theme.

title_template.description: How a page's title is written in the browser tab and in search results; {title} is the page's own title and {site_name} the site name.
title_template.title: Title Template
title_template.x-summary: How a page's title is written in the browser tab, using {title} and {site_name}.

admin_cookie_insecure.description: Send the admin session cookie over plain HTTP. Only for local development without TLS; a production deployment must never set it.
admin_cookie_insecure.title: Admin Cookie Insecure
admin_cookie_insecure.x-summary: Only for local development without TLS; never turn it on in production.

api_base_url.description: Base URL of the Flask API's /api mount point (for example https://example.org/api). The update asks it whether the site answers, and web/lib/apiclient.py calls it outside the Flask app. There is no default: nothing guesses a loopback address, so it must be set for either to work.
api_base_url.title: Api Base Url
api_base_url.x-summary: Where the API lives; the update's health check asks it. No default.

base_url.description: The address this site is reached at, as an absolute http or https address with a trailing slash. Canonical links, link previews, the sitemap and emailed links are built from it, never from the request's Host header.
base_url.title: Base Url
base_url.x-summary: The public address of the site, used for canonical links, previews and the sitemap.

config_version.description: The settings file format version; a file without one is version 1.
config_version.title: Config Version
config_version.x-summary: Which format version this settings file is in; the program keeps it up to date.

control_database.description: The MySQL schema holding admin identities, sessions, API keys and the audit log. Never listed or selectable as a galaxy.
control_database.title: Control Database
control_database.x-summary: The database that holds admin accounts, sessions, API keys and the audit log.

debug.description: Debug mode: every decision the generator makes, every random roll, every SQL statement, queue event and request, written to the console of each planetgen command (stdout) and to log_file. The output is large.
debug.title: Debug
debug.x-summary: Write a very detailed log of everything the generator does; it grows fast.

debug_areas.description: Limit debug mode to some areas of output: decision, draw, sql, queue, cache, web, lib (comma separated; a leading - leaves one out). Empty writes everything but branch, which logs every conditional jump of the program's own code and is written only when named.
debug_areas.title: Debug Areas
debug_areas.x-summary: Which kinds of detail debug mode writes; empty is all of them.

log_dir.description: The folder of the always-on activity log; empty means /var/log/planetgen on Linux, /Library/Logs/planetgen on macOS.
log_dir.title: Log Dir
log_dir.x-summary: The folder that holds the always-on activity log.

log_file.title: Log File
log_file.x-summary: The file the debug log is written to.

log_rotation.description: How the activity log is rotated: system (logrotate or newsyslog), app (the program, 100 MB per file, 30 old copies) or auto (system where an installed rotation config exists, else app).
log_rotation.title: Log Rotation
log_rotation.x-summary: Who trims old activity logs: the system, the program, or whichever is installed.

login_allowlist.description: Client addresses or networks (CIDR) never locked out after failed logins; loopback never is either. Environment: comma- or space-separated.
login_allowlist.title: Login Allowlist
login_allowlist.x-summary: Client addresses or networks that are never locked out after failed logins.

record_file.description: A file every log line of a planetgen command is also written to as a record: one per line, the time in UTC. Empty writes none; the --record-file option does the same for one command.
record_file.title: Record File
record_file.x-summary: A file that gets every log line as a machine-readable record, for a tool to read.

record_format.description: The form of the record file's lines: logfmt (key=value) or json (one object per line).
record_format.title: Record Format
record_format.x-summary: Whether the record file is written as key=value lines or as JSON lines.

secret_key.description: Signs the CSRF tokens on the pages' forms. Empty makes one and keeps it in the state folder (mode 0600), so every worker and restart shares it.
secret_key.title: Secret Key
secret_key.x-summary: Signs the security tokens on forms; empty makes a random one at each start.

site_name.description: Display name for this deployment, shown in the header, the home page heading, every page title and the footer.
site_name.title: Site Name
site_name.x-summary: The name shown in the header, the home page, page titles and the footer.
